articles.title: US, Iranian military issue contesting claims over control of Strait of Hormuz
articles.summary:
US, Iranian military issue contesting claims over control of Strait of Hormuz

US Central Command (Centcom) dismissed "Iranian claims" to control the Strait of Hormuz, alleging that the US and its regional partners "control the strait as commercial vessels continue to transit despite unwarranted... aggression" from Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC).

In a post on X on Thursday, Centcom also denied that the IRGC had killed hundreds of US service members in Jordan and that a Singapore-flagged container ship struck a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday.

Meanwhile, Iran's IRIB news reported that Iranian army commander Amir Hatami said the strait is under “full surveillance” by the army and the IRGC, adding that “not a single enemy vessel has been able to enter the maritime space of Oman and the Strait of Hormuz.”

articles.title: White House prepares plans to use 'mother of all bombs' on Iran, says official
articles.summary:
White House prepares plans to use 'mother of all bombs' on Iran, says official

The White House has prepared plans to use a Massive Ordnance Air Blast, dubbed "mother of all bombs", to hit military sites in Iran if ordered by US President Donald Trump, sources familiar with the matter told CBS News on Thursday.

"The Department of War plans for a wide range of operational scenarios to execute Presidential and Secretary level direction and to ensure mission success in any operational environment," a Pentagon Official was quoted as saying by the outlet.

This comes after Trump said the US would not attack Iran before the midterm elections and touted "productive conversations" with Iran, without providing specifics, last week.

articles.title: Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s cell phone confiscated, family members subpoenaed
articles.summary:
Congresswoman Ilhan Omar’s cell phone confiscated, family members subpoenaed

Submitted by MEE staff on Thu, 10/15/2026 - 20:21
Critics have called the investigation a witch hunt, citing President Donald Trump's past remarks to 'send her back' to Somalia
A supporter holds a placard during a rally for Democratic US Representative Ilhan Omar in Minneapolis, Minnesota, on 12 October 2026 (Tim Evans/Reuters)
Off

The US Department of Justice (DOJ), whose chief, Todd Blanche, was formerly President Donald Trump's personal lawyer, has subpoenaed the relatives of Minnesota Democratic Congresswoman Ilhan Omar as part of its investigation into alleged immigration fraud, The Minnesota Star Tribune reported on Thursday. 

The relatives do not include her husband and daughter.

Federal agents from Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) on Monday carried out a pre-dawn raid on Omar's Washington, DC, home, and it has now been revealed that her cell phone, laptop, and other devices were confiscated in the process.

Omar has been a frequent target of Trump since his first term in office, when she was elected to the US House of Representatives in 2018.

Born in Somalia, she arrived in the US in 1995 as a child refugee, and became the first hijab-wearing Muslim to serve in the US Congress. She is up for re-election again on 3 November. 

She obtained US citizenship at 17 after her now-deceased father was naturalised. The DOJ is reportedly looking into whether she was actually 18 at the time, meaning she would have had to apply for citizenship separately from her parents. 

Trump has repeatedly called for an investigation into whether she is a lawful citizen, and even claimed she married her own brother for immigration purposes. Omar has denied these allegations, but both the president and Vice President JD Vance have insisted for the past year that she should be investigated, and Trump has led chants of "send her back" at his rallies. 

On Wednesday, The Wall Street Journal, citing unnamed US officials, said the administration is building a case to strip Omar of her citizenship and deport her. 

Dozens to be stripped of US citizenship

In an unprecedented move, the DOJ announced last week it would move to strip 40 people of their US citizenship. Such an act has usually been rare and focused on fewer than a handful of Americans per presidential administration.

But it is also part of Trump's wide-ranging efforts to deport up to one million people a year from the US, regardless of whether they employed legal or illegal immigration pathways. 

Immigration agents raid home of Congresswoman Ilhan Omar
Read More »

Omar has been a fierce critic of the president, but far from the loudest or most prominent.

Former Republican Congresswoman turned Trump foe Marjorie Taylor-Greene said on X that, like many of Omar's supporters, she also believes the investigation is a distraction.

"Me and Ilhan Omar are far apart policy wise. I’m pro life, she’s pro abortion. I’m pro 2A, she’s pro gun control. And on and on," Greene wrote on Wednesday. 

"But can someone tell me how pretending to get ready to deport Ilhan Omar is going to bring gas down under $2, make health insurance freaking affordable, make a family’s weekly grocery bill make sense, and stop sending our beloved military off to fight for another fucking foreign war???"

"People are so sick and tired of the bullshit," she said.

This is not the first time Omar has come under investigation. In 2022, the former administration of Joe Biden, a Democrat, began looking into her finances, but that investigation ultimately stalled due to a lack of evidence, The New York Times reported.

Palestinian commission documents 21 Israeli attacks against farmers in 12 hours
articles.summary:
Palestinian commission documents 21 Israeli attacks against farmers in 12 hours

The Colonisation and Wall Resistance Commission (CWRC) said on Thursday that it had documented 21 attacks carried out by Israeli forces and settlers against Palestinian farmers and their lands in the last 12 hours, Wafa reported.

According to the CWRC, the attacks were recorded in the governorates of Nablus, Ramallah and al-Bireh, Hebron, Jerusalem, Jenin and Salfit in the occupied West Bank.

They included 13 incidents carried out by Israeli settlers, some under the protection of the Israeli army, and eight incidents carried out by Israeli forces, ranging from physical assaults, detention and arrest to forcing farmers to leave their lands, stealing crops and uprooting trees.

archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující napětí v Hormuzském průlivu a zvýšenou nervozitu na trzích s ropou a hnojivy. Politická a bezpečnostní nestabilita v Izraeli a Gaze zůstane na vysoké úrovni.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued tension in the Strait of Hormuz and heightened nervousness in oil and fertilizer markets are expected. Political and security instability in Israel and Gaza will remain elevated.

archive.security_status_cs: V regionu nadále eskalují vnitřní i vnější konflikty, včetně cílených atentátů na představitelé íránských ozbrojených složek a pokračujících střetů v Gaze. Politická nestabilita v Izraeli roste kvůli blížícím se volbám a ostrým střetům mezi politickými a bezpečnostními špičkami. Irák mezitím přistoupil k devalvaci dináru kvůli vnitřním finančním potížím.
archive.security_status_en: Internal and external conflicts continue to escalate across the region, including targeted assassinations of Iranian security personnel and ongoing clashes in Gaza. Political instability in Israel is rising due to upcoming elections and sharp clashes between political and defense leadership. Meanwhile, Iraq has devalued its dinar to cope with domestic financial strains.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další politickou polarizaci v Izraeli v souvislosti s předvolebním bojovým a přetrvávající napětí v Íránu. Energetické a komoditní trhy budou nadále citlivě reagovat na bezpečnostní incidenty v regionu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further political polarization in Israel related to the pre-election campaign and ongoing tensions in Iran are expected. Energy and commodity markets will continue to react sensitively to security incidents in the region.

archive.security_status_cs: Bezpečnostní situace v regionu zůstává vysoce napjatá kvůli eskalujícím hrozbám vůči Íránu, incidentům v Hormuzském průlivu a přetrvávajícím střetům v Libanonu a na Západním břehu. Diplomatické snahy USA a regionálních aktérů nedokázaly zcela utlumit riziko širší konfrontace.
archive.security_status_en: The regional security situation remains highly tense due to escalating threats against Iran, incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and ongoing clashes in Lebanon and the West Bank. Diplomatic efforts by the US and regional actors have failed to fully mitigate the risk of a broader confrontation.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat další diplomatické manévry ohledně Íránu a zvýšenou nervozitu na trzích s energetickými komoditami. Politické napětí uvnitř Izraele a USA bude nadále ovlivňovat regionální stabilitu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, further diplomatic maneuvers regarding Iran and heightened nervousness in energy commodity markets are expected. Political tensions within Israel and the US will continue to influence regional stability.

archive.security_status_cs: Napětí v regionu prudce eskaluje kvůli přímým vojenským hrozbám vůči Íránu, incidentům v Hormuzském průlivu a politickým tlakům na Libanon. Vnitřní nestabilita v Izraeli a Gaze spolu s kybernetickými útoky na novináře nadále prohlubují bezpečnostní rizika.
archive.security_status_en: Regional tensions are escalating sharply due to direct military threats against Iran, incidents in the Strait of Hormuz, and political pressure on Lebanon. Internal instability in Israel and Gaza, alongside cyberattacks on journalists, continue to deepen security risks.
archive.forecast_cs: V nejbližších dnech lze očekávat pokračující eskalaci rétoriky kolem Íránu a zvýšenou ostražitost v oblasti námořní dopravy v Zálivu. Diplomatické tlaky na Izrael a Libanon budou nadále zatěžovat regionální stabilitu.
archive.forecast_en: Over the coming days, continued escalation of rhetoric surrounding Iran and heightened vigilance in Gulf shipping lanes are expected. Diplomatic pressures on Israel and Lebanon will continue to strain regional stability.
